sections.markdown:
## C2 — Interstates, road markings and railroad crossings
FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Pavement markings help identify the correct vehicle position on the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
An overhead lane arrow with ONLY requires travel in the arrow's indicated direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
An arrow painted on the roadway has the same directional meaning as an overhead arrow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
On a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, drive on the right and leave the left half to opposing traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A01
On a multilane road, select the lane with the smoothest traffic flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
With three or more lanes traveling one direction, the middle lane or lanes usually have the smoothest flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A01
The source describes the left lane as serving faster traffic, passing and left turns. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A01
Slower traffic and drivers turning right use the right lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A01
With two lanes traveling one direction, the right lane usually has the smoothest flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A01
Where special left-turn lanes exist, the left lane may have the smoothest traffic flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A01
White road lines separate traffic traveling in the same direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A01
Yellow road lines separate traffic traveling in opposite directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A01
A broken line allows passing or a lane change when the way is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A01
A solid white line indicates that passing or changing lanes is hazardous. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A01
A solid yellow line bars passing or lane changing except for a left turn into or out of an alley, private road or driveway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A02
The handbook's marking example prohibits passing when a solid yellow line is on the driver's side. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A02
The handbook's opposing-side solid-yellow passing example still requires the way ahead to be clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A02
Double yellow lines separating traffic prohibit passing in the handbook's example. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A03
At an advance railroad warning, slow down, look and listen, and prepare to stop if a train approaches. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A03
The railroad approach marking described is R-X-R followed by a stop line nearer the tracks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A03
Wait behind the marked stop line while a train passes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A03
A railroad crossbuck functions as a yield sign requiring drivers to yield to trains. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A03
At a crossbuck, slow down, look and listen, and stop when a train is approaching. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A03
A sign below a crossbuck indicates the track count where more than one track is present. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A03
Stop for flashing red railroad signals and yield to the approaching train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A03
At a crossing with multiple tracks, verify that every track is clear before crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A03
When crossing lights begin flashing, stop before the place where the gate will lower across the lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-R28 | anchor: A03
Remain stopped until the crossing gates are raised and the warning lights have stopped flashing, then cross only when safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0066]
